episodes.title: The Date He Should Not Know

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: That photograph proves only one thing. Meera left Dharmapur with me because she wanted to abandon her marriage and her children.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Let me ask him one question.

lines.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
lines.text: You will speak when the committee permits it.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: This is a police verification, not a punishment meeting. She may question the man in the photograph.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Certainly. A truthful man does not fear questions.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Where was this photograph taken?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Kota bus stand.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Which platform?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: There are no platforms at that counter. Only benches.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: So you recognise the place.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: I have worked in transport for twelve years. I recognise hundreds of counters.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Ask why my daughter was standing beside him.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Your daughter? Yesterday, I was a stranger bringing scandal to your courtyard.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: He called her an impostor inside the police station.

lines.speaker: SECOND VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: Now he needs her to be his daughter, because the photograph is public.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: The committee did not summon the street to judge me.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: No. The evidence did.

lines.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
lines.text: Raghav, explain the photograph from the beginning.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Meera approached me privately. She said she was unhappy at home. She asked for transport to Kota.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: That is a lie.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: You asked me to speak. Please allow me the courtesy of finishing.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Courtesy? You watched while I was taken away.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Meera, taken by whom?

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I don't... I did not know his name then. Raghav spoke to him near the tea counter.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: She means Shahid. He was arranging labour transport that week.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: You know which man she means without hearing a description.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Because she has made this accusation before. Confused stories travel quickly in a village.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I have not spoken Shahid's name in this village.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Then perhaps your story reached Dharmapur before you did.

lines.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
lines.text: Answer plainly. Did Meera travel with you willingly?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Yes. She sat beside me for three hours. She drank tea. She could have called for help.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You kept my phone.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: You said your battery had failed.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You removed the battery.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Modern phones do not have removable batteries. Listen to how her memory changes.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: It was my old blue phone. The back cover was tied with tape.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: She had a blue phone like that.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Many people did.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Hers had white tape across the back. I put it there.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: A daughter repeating a detail does not prove force.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: Why would Ma leave without us?

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Mohan, don't call her that here.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: You cannot stop me thinking it.

lines.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
lines.text: Children should be taken inside.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: They are the children Raghav says she abandoned. Their presence is relevant.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: It is also cruel. Tara's school is close to the transport yard, isn't it? Public gossip can be difficult for a girl her age.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Do not bring my daughter's school into your mouth.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: I was expressing concern.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Powerful men often call a warning concern. Continue with your account.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Meera wanted work in Kota. She said her family watched every rupee. She said she wanted a life where nobody counted her steps.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I wanted to buy Tara exam guides and Mohan new sandals. That is what I told you.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: You told me many things.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Then tell them what happened after the bus stand.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: You left with Shahid.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You put me in his vehicle.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: I introduced two adults. I did not put anyone anywhere.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Was money discussed?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Transport costs money.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: That was not my question.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: No illegal payment was discussed in my presence.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: He counted notes inside the vehicle.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: She was outside the vehicle. Now she was inside. Another change.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I was beside the open door. I saw bundles under the front seat.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Bundles can contain invoices. Transport businesses still use paper.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Meera, if this happened, why did you not return?

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Because I was not allowed to return.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: For eighteen months? Not one message? Not one neighbour?

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Baba, I tried—

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Do not use that word to make an answer disappear.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: She came back. That is an answer.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: The boy has more sense than this committee.

lines.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
lines.text: Silence, or I will clear the courtyard.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Raghav, did you receive money for arranging Meera's travel?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: A small brokerage fee. Legal and ordinary.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Two thousand rupees, perhaps. It was a long time ago.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: That is not the payment he is afraid of.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: There. An accusation without a number, a receipt or a witness.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Did Shahid pay you?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Did anyone connected to Shahid transfer money to you, your business or your relatives?

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: You may inspect every account for which you have legal authority.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Ask him when it happened.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: When did what happen?

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: The payment. He knows the date.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: This is becoming theatrical.

lines.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
lines.text: Then end the theatre. Give the committee the date of your two-thousand-rupee brokerage.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: I cannot remember an ordinary fee after eighteen months.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: But you remember how long she sat, where she stood and what she said about her family.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: Because those details became important later.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: The larger payment was important immediately.

lines.speaker: RAGHAV
lines.text: There was no larger payment. The five lakh rupees were not even paid to me. They were paid on the third of May, twenty twenty-one.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Meera has not told police the amount. She only reported that money changed hands.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Yet you have just named the exact five-lakh payment date before Meera told police either the amount or the date.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: This door. Break this door, and I will show you where they kept me.
lines.sfx_cue: metal latch rattling, fists striking wooden door

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Nobody breaks my property. Show me a warrant or leave my courtyard.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Open the room. Refuse again, and I will seal the entire floor until a magistrate decides who enters it.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: You police people arrive after eighteen months and speak as though dust committed the crime.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I slept behind that door. I counted the cracks above the window every night.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I have never rented a room to any Meera.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Then we have travelled to Kota for another false memory.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: She knew the staircase without anyone showing her.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: That does not mean she lived here.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: There are seventeen steps. The sixth one is broken at the edge. The room has a green wall and no fan regulator.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Every room upstairs has a green wall.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: And the broken sixth step?

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: People notice stairs while climbing them.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: There is a water stain shaped like a hook beside the window.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Enough. The room was rented to another woman.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Name.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Sarla.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: That is what Shahid called me in front of strangers.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I do not know any Shahid.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: You answered before I asked whether you knew him.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Because she has repeated the name three times in my courtyard.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Madam, open the room. Either her details are correct, or we end this journey here.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You are waiting for me to fail.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: I am waiting for evidence that does not change whenever a new person arrives.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: If she is wrong about one stain, will you take her away?

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: No. One room does not decide her identity.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Good. Then decide it somewhere else.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Constable, call the local station and request a property seal.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Wait. There is no need to spoil everyone's day over one empty room.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: It was not empty when you collected rent.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I collected rent from Sarla's guardian.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Guardian? She was an adult tenant.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: That was the word he used.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Who was he?

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: A transport man. I do not remember every customer.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You remember enough to change the word landlord into guardian.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I remember rent paid on time. That is all.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The lock opened. Meera stepped inside before anyone invited her.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: The cot was against this wall.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: It is against the other wall now.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Move it. Please. There should be writing behind the headboard.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: There is no writing. I repaint between tenants.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You did not repaint behind the cot.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Constable, move it carefully.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: There are lines on the wall.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Thirty-four vertical marks. Some crossed in groups of seven.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I marked the nights when he took the outside bolt off.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Anyone could make marks.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: The last group stops halfway because Shahid came early.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: She is inventing meaning for scratches.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Then tell me why this bedroom door has an outside bolt.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: For luggage security.

lines.speaker: VOICE FROM COURTYARD
lines.text: Luggage does not sleep in the room and cry at night.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Who said that? Come upstairs and give your name.

lines.speaker: SECOND VOICE FROM COURTYARD
lines.text: We all heard someone. None of us wants our name in your ledger.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: They heard me.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: They heard a person. I will take individual statements before deciding more.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Look above the window. The hook-shaped stain.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: It is there.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Stains survive tenants. It could be older than her claim.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: Why do you make every correct answer smaller?

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Because you are a child, and somebody must protect you from wanting too much.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: I only want Ma.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: You want this woman to be Ma.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: She knows things Ma knew.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Things can be told.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Tara is right to be afraid.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Do not tell me what I feel.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Then I won't.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Meera, what else should be in this room? Something removable, not a wall or stain.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: A brass button under the window ledge. I pushed it into a crack.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Now we will search for buttons in an old building?

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Yes. Evidence is often smaller than the person hiding it.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Why a brass button?

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: It came off Mohan's brown sweater. I found it in my blouse pocket after they brought me here.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: The sweater with the bear?

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: No. The one you hated. Brown wool, wooden train stitched near the collar.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: It scratched my neck.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You cried whenever I pulled it over your ears.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: What did you sing?

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Mohan, not here.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: What did you sing when I would not put my head through?

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Little train, little train, wait beside the door. Mohan has one stubborn head, but Ma has counted four.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: No. You missed the next part.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I don't... I thought you had forgotten it.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: Sing it properly.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: One for anger, one for tears, one that asks for sweets. The fourth comes out when morning starts, and kisses both my cheeks.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: Ma.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Mohan—

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: She is my Ma. I am saying it where everybody can hear me. She is my Ma.

lines.speaker: VOICE FROM COURTYARD
lines.text: The boy has recognised his mother.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: A lullaby proves memory, not identity.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: Then my memory is better than yours.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: I found the crack beneath the ledge.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: There is no button. But the plaster has been disturbed recently.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Repairs happen. You cannot arrest a wall.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Where is the rental ledger?

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: You have seen the room. Leave my records alone.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The room was rented under another name. The ledger is now part of the verification.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Old books are downstairs. Some pages may be damaged.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: If one page is missing, the entire ledger goes into evidence.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Downstairs, the landlord opened a steel trunk and lifted out a red cloth book.
lines.sfx_cue: steel trunk lid opening, paper rustling

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Here. Sarla. Room twelve. Rent paid in cash.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The tenant column contains a different name, but this signature does not say Sarla.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: That is my name.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: No. No, that date cannot be right.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Read it aloud.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Twenty-first of June, twenty twenty-one.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: By then, our family believed Meera had already been cremated.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: And beside that date, the rental ledger contains Meera's signature.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Nobody touches the evidence table. The first person who crosses this rope leaves the verification.
lines.sfx_cue: crowd pressing against rope, police whistle

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Then remove Mohan. He is already beside her chair.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: I will sit with my Ma.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: He may sit there. He may not touch the documents.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I want my death certificate placed in front of me.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: It is an official record, not an object for public handling.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Place it inside the transparent cover, Babulal.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: If the cover tears, I will record who ordered this.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Record my designation correctly.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: Yesterday she was locked outside her house. Today her death certificate gets a police chair.

lines.speaker: SECOND VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: Paper has always received more respect than women here.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: This is supposed to be evidence, not entertainment.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Correct. That is why you will not interrupt each item.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: One hour earlier, a sealed fingerprint envelope had fallen through the station slot into an empty records room. Nobody saw it arrive.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Now Kavita placed that envelope beside the certificate recording Meera as dead.
lines.sfx_cue: paper envelope placed on wooden table

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The open verification has five parts. Documents. Fingerprints. Family testimony. Physical identifiers. Contradictory records.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: And no final declaration until every objection is entered.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Agreed. Read the first document.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: School admission register. Student name, Meera. Father's name, Devraj. Original left-thumb impression attached.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: That register is old. Ink spreads.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Your objection is noted before the result has even been opened.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: He is frightened.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: I am frightened of another mistake being made in public.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: The first mistake was made in public too. You called a burned body your daughter, then called your living daughter a stranger.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: She has spoken the truth plainly.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: You saw no face in that hospital either.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: I was not asked to identify the body.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Enough. Babulal, the second document.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: Ration-card amendment form. Signed by Meera. Right-thumb impression taken two years before her disappearance.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The forensic unit compared both archived impressions with the fresh prints taken at the station.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Was the unit told what result the police expected?

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The samples were coded. The examiner received no names.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: What does the envelope say?

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: You may come closer, Tara. Do not cross the rope.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: I can hear from here.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The fresh left-thumb impression matches the school register impression at fourteen corresponding ridge characteristics.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: Fourteen points. Say what that means.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: It means the old and new left-thumb impressions were made by the same person.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: Ma's thumb remembers her, even if Nana does not.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: A child should not humiliate his grandfather before a crowd.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: You humiliated Ma before a bigger crowd.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Mohan, sit down.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: I am sitting.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Then sit quietly.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: All right, Ma.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The right-thumb impression also matches the ration-card form.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: Both archived documents existed before the disappearance. Their dates and storage entries are verified.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: What about the Kota ledger? It carries her signature after the cremation.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: That is the contradictory-record section. We will reach it.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Conveniently last.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Conveniently in the order I announced before you objected.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Physical identifiers. Meera, show both hands.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: The tattoo is on my left hand. It has always been on my left hand.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: The hospital photograph shows the burned body's tattoo beside the right wrist.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The photograph number and hospital intake number are legible. There is no reversal in the image.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: The black thread looked identical.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: A black wrist thread is not unique. A tattoo on the opposite hand is a material discrepancy.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: You did not touch the body, Baba. You would not even touch my hand at the station.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: The body was burned. I was told not to disturb it.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Who told you?

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: A hospital worker. I don't... there were several people speaking at once.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Name or description?

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Then your statement remains that an unidentified worker discouraged a physical check.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: I was grieving.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: And I was alive.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Family testimony. Tara, what did Meera know inside the house?

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: She knew where my first school ribbon was hidden.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Someone could have told her.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: I did not tell anyone the tin was behind the loose brick.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Did she find it without directions?

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Do you recognise her as your mother?

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: I recognise things she knows. I am not ready to say more.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: She does not have to say more today.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Mohan?

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: She sang the sweater song. Only Ma knew the fourth head kisses both her cheeks.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Did she prompt you?

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: No. I tested her, and she finished it.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: He called her Ma in Kota. We all heard about it.

lines.speaker: MOHAN
lines.text: I will call her Ma here too. Ma. Ma. Ma.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The repetition is unnecessary, but the answer is recorded.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Let him repeat it. They repeated that I was dead for eighteen months.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Now the Kota rental ledger.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: The tenant name is Sarla. The signature appears to say Meera. The date is the twenty-first of June, twenty twenty-one.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Meera provided six fresh signatures under observation this morning.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: A person can alter a signature.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Yes. That is why the examiner also compared letter formation, pressure and stroke order with older records.

lines.speaker: TARA
lines.text: And?

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The Kota signature appears copied. Its strokes stop and restart where Meera's natural signature remains continuous.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Someone signed my name.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: That is the present forensic opinion. The ledger does not disprove your identity.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Opinion is not certainty.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Neither was your identification of the body, yet it was accepted as certainty.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: Madam, the register cannot simply be rewritten during a village meeting.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: I am not ordering a rewrite. I am ordering the death certificate marked disputed pending formal correction and further inquiry.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: That requires recorded grounds.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Record them. Two fingerprint matches. Correct private family knowledge. A physical tattoo discrepancy. A copied rental signature. Consistent identification of the Kota room.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: You are declaring her genuine because the crowd wants a miracle.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: No. I am announcing that the evidence strongly supports Meera being alive and genuine.

lines.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
lines.text: Say it again. Let the people at the back hear.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The woman standing here is strongly supported by documentary, fingerprint and family evidence as Meera.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Babulal, bring me the paper that buried my name.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: It remains government property.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Then let the government correct itself where everyone can see.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: I have a red disputed-record seal. Once stamped, the certificate cannot be used as an uncontested proof of death.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Apply it.

lines.speaker: DEVRAJ
lines.text: Wait. If you stamp that, the original murder case—

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: Will be reviewed on evidence. Not protected from embarrassment.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: The seal is inked.

lines.speaker: MEERA
lines.text: Do it.

lines.speaker: KAVITA
lines.text: The police officially acknowledge that the original identification of the burned body may have been wrong.

lines.speaker: BABULAL
lines.text: Meera's death certificate is now sealed and formally marked disputed.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Raghav publicly asserted that Meera willingly travelled with him to Kota because she wanted to leave her family.

state_changes.fact: Publicly gives an explanation for the bus stand photograph.
Is publicly accused of abandoning her children.

beat_sheet.note: Raghav's account is an assertion and is not established as true.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Meera asserted that Raghav took her phone battery, placed her with Shahid and witnessed money being counted.

state_changes.fact: Is publicly connected by Meera to Shahid and an alleged payment.
Is named in Meera's allegation about her movement from the bus stand.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Tara confirmed that Meera previously owned the taped blue phone described during the confrontation.

state_changes.fact: Receives limited public corroboration from Tara.
Publicly corroborates one detail without recognising Meera as her mother.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Raghav named a five-lakh-rupee payment date before Meera had disclosed the amount or date to police.

state_changes.fact: Reveals knowledge of the alleged payment that his prior account did not explain.
Obtains a material contradiction in Raghav's public statement.

beat_sheet.location: Kota rental building courtyard and room twelve
beat_sheet.what_happened: Meera identified room twelve as the place where she said she had been confined, while the landlord stated that it had been rented to a woman named Sarla.

state_changes.fact: Locates the specific Kota room connected to her allegation.
Names the tenant as Sarla rather than Meera.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Inside room twelve, Meera correctly predicted wall marks, a hook-shaped water stain and an outside door bolt.

state_changes.fact: Demonstrates detailed prior knowledge of room twelve.
Gains physical corroboration for part of Meera's Kota account.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Meera completed Mohan's private childhood lullaby, and Mohan publicly called her Ma.

state_changes.fact: Is publicly recognised as mother by Mohan for the first time.
Commits publicly to recognising Meera as his mother.
Faces public contradiction from Mohan while continuing to resist Meera's identity.

beat_sheet.what_happened: The rental ledger contained Meera's name as a signature beside 2021-06-21, when her family believed she had already been cremated.

state_changes.fact: Contains a disputed signature in Meera's name after her presumed cremation.
Takes responsibility for resolving a new documentary contradiction.

beat_sheet.location: Dharmapur police station empty records room
beat_sheet.what_happened: A sealed forensic fingerprint result arrived in the empty records room before the public verification.

state_changes.fact: Arrives sealed and available for the identity verification.

beat_sheet.note: No cast character witnessed the delivery because the records room was empty; Kavita later retrieved and opened the sealed result publicly.

beat_sheet.location: Dharmapur police station public verification area
beat_sheet.what_happened: Kavita publicly established that Meera's fresh fingerprints matched two archived documents created before her disappearance.

state_changes.fact: Receives strong forensic support for her identity.
Loses a major basis for publicly rejecting Meera.
Links the returned woman to Meera's archived records.

beat_sheet.location: Dharmapur police station public verification area
beat_sheet.what_happened: The public verification combined the tattoo-hand discrepancy, family testimony, room knowledge and an examiner's opinion that the Kota signature had been copied.

state_changes.fact: No longer operates as reliable evidence against Meera's identity.
Confirms Meera's private knowledge but withholds full maternal recognition.
Again recognises Meera as his mother in public.

beat_sheet.location: Dharmapur police station public verification area
beat_sheet.what_happened: Kavita announced that the evidence strongly supported Meera being alive and genuine, and Babulal sealed her death certificate as disputed while police acknowledged the original identification might have been wrong.

state_changes.fact: Gains formal police support for her claim to be alive and genuine.
Is formally marked disputed.
Publicly acknowledges that the original body identification may have been wrong.
His body identification is formally placed in doubt.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: How can Meera restore her identity when the register records her as dead?
promise_ledger.how_paid: Fingerprint, document and family evidence publicly supported Meera's identity, and her death certificate was formally sealed as disputed.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Will either of Meera's children publicly recognize her as their mother?
promise_ledger.how_paid: Meera completed Mohan's private childhood lullaby, and he publicly called her Ma in the Kota rental building.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Why are four men imprisoned for murdering a woman who is alive?
Whose body was cremated after being wrongly identified as Meera?
What explanation will Raghav give for being photographed beside Meera?
promise_ledger.how_paid: Raghav publicly claimed Meera willingly travelled with him to Kota because she wanted to abandon her family.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: How did Raghav know the exact five-lakh-rupee payment date before Meera disclosed the amount?
Will the signature in the Kota rental ledger disprove Meera's identity?
promise_ledger.how_paid: The examiner found that the ledger signature appeared copied and did not match the continuous stroke pattern in Meera's genuine signatures.

dates_fixed.what: Meera enters Dharmapur police station and discovers that she remains recorded as dead.
Kavita conducts the initial private identity test and finds the tattoo-hand discrepancy.
Meera visits her former house under police guard and the bus stand photograph arrives.
Raghav gives his account before the village committee and reveals knowledge of a payment dated 2021-05-03.
Meera identifies room twelve in Kota, Mohan publicly calls her Ma and the rental ledger reveals a disputed signature dated 2021-06-21.
Kavita conducts the open identity verification and Meera's death certificate is marked disputed.

periods_fixed.elapsed: No time elapsed; both episodes occur on 2022-11-14.
